info.description:
# Performance Monitor Infrastructure API for MCP Servers

This comprehensive API provides advanced network performance monitoring capabilities specifically optimized for MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers and automated monitoring systems.
The API enables sophisticated monitoring of device health, performance metrics, and network analytics across various network components with intelligent automation support.

## MCP Server Integration Features
- **Automated Performance Monitoring**: Continuous collection and analysis of network performance metrics
- **Intelligent Alerting**: AI-driven anomaly detection and automated alert generation
- **Time-Series Analytics**: Advanced time-series data processing for trend analysis and forecasting
- **Real-time Health Monitoring**: Live device health status tracking with automated response capabilities
- **Scalable Data Collection**: High-performance metric collection supporting thousands of devices
- **Integration-Ready**: Designed for seamless integration with monitoring platforms and automation tools

## Key Features
- **Application Discovery**: List supported monitoring applications and their capabilities
- **Metric Collection**: Retrieve time-series performance data from network devices with advanced filtering
- **Device Health Analytics**: Monitor device health status and performance indicators with trend analysis
- **Flexible Filtering**: Advanced filtering and pagination optimized for large-scale monitoring deployments
- **Real-time Data**: Access to current and historical performance metrics with microsecond precision
- **Bulk Operations**: Efficient batch processing for monitoring large network infrastructures

## MCP Use Cases
- **Infrastructure Monitoring**: Automated monitoring of switches, routers, and network devices
- **Performance Optimization**: AI-driven performance analysis and optimization recommendations
- **Capacity Planning**: Predictive analytics for network capacity planning and resource allocation
- **Anomaly Detection**: Machine learning-based anomaly detection for proactive issue identification
- **Compliance Monitoring**: Automated compliance tracking for SLA and performance requirements
- **Integration Workflows**: Seamless integration with ITSM, SIEM, and automation platforms

## Supported Applications
Currently supports monitoring for:
- **Network Infrastructure**: Switches, routers, and network devices with full SNMP and telemetry support
- **Device Stats**: CPU, memory, temperature, and power metrics with threshold monitoring
- **Interface Stats**: Port utilization, errors, and performance data with trend analysis
- **Wireless Stats**: Wireless device and interface monitoring with RF analytics
- **Health Analytics**: Comprehensive device health scoring and predictive maintenance
- **Usage Capacity Analytics**: Comprehensive usage and capacity monitoring across network infrastructure

## Data Formats
All timestamps use ISO 8601 UTC format (e.g., "2024-08-26T19:00:00Z").
Pagination is supported across all list operations for efficient data retrieval.
Time-series data includes microsecond precision for high-frequency monitoring.

## Authentication
This API requires proper authentication and authorization. Contact your system administrator for access credentials.

get.summary: Get the complete metric capability schema for all groups
get.description:
Returns the full metric registry in a single call — all metric groups, sub-metrics,
field names, types, units, supported filters, and example requests.

**This is the recommended first call for any AI agent or automation system**

post.summary: Advanced Time-Series Metric Retrieval for MCP Servers
post.description:
**High-Performance Time-Series Data Retrieval for MCP Servers**

Retrieves comprehensive time-series metric data from monitored network devices with advanced filtering,
intelligent pagination, and optimized time range processing. This primary data endpoint is specifically
designed for MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers implementing sophisticated performance monitoring,
analytics, and automated alerting systems.

**MCP Server Features:**
- **High-Performance Time-Series Processing**: Optimized queries for large-scale monitoring deployments
- **Intelligent Data Sampling**: Configurable sampling rates for efficient data processing and storage
- **Real-Time and Historical Analytics**: Support for both live monitoring and historical trend analysis
- **Single Device Per Request**: Exactly one device per request; issue parallel requests for multi-device scenarios
- **Automated Filtering**: Advanced pattern matching for interface and metric-specific data extraction
- **Scalable Pagination**: Optimized pagination for processing massive datasets in monitoring workflows

**Advanced Time-Series Capabilities:**
- **Microsecond Precision**: High-resolution timestamps for precise performance analysis
- **Multi-Dimensional Filtering**: Complex filtering across time, devices, interfaces, and metric types
- **Adaptive Sampling**: Intelligent data sampling based on monitoring requirements and system load
- **Stream Processing Ready**: Optimized for real-time stream processing and event-driven analytics
- **Memory Efficient**: Optimized data structures for handling large time-series datasets

**MCP Use Cases:**
- **Automated Performance Monitoring**: Continuous monitoring with intelligent threshold detection
- **Anomaly Detection Systems**: Time-series data for machine learning-based anomaly detection
- **Capacity Planning Analytics**: Historical data analysis for predictive capacity planning
- **Real-Time Alerting**: Live data feeds for immediate alert generation and response automation
- **Trend Analysis Engines**: Long-term trend analysis for performance optimization and planning
- **Integration Workflows**: Data feeds for ITSM, SIEM, and automation platform integration

**Enhanced Time Range Options:**
1. **Absolute Range**: Precise time windows for specific analysis periods with timezone support
2. **Duration from Start**: Forward-looking analysis for performance trending and forecasting
3. **Duration to End**: Backward-looking analysis for incident investigation and root cause analysis
4. **Recent Data**: Real-time monitoring with configurable recent data windows
5. **Latest Values**: Immediate access to current state for real-time dashboards and alerting
6. **Sliding Windows**: Continuous monitoring with rolling time windows for trend detection

**Device Selection (Single Device Per Request):**
- **UUID-Based Identification**: Preferred method for consistent device tracking across system changes
- **Flexible ID Mapping**: Support for internal IDs and serial numbers for legacy system integration
- **One Device Per Request**: Each request must specify exactly one device; comma-separated lists are rejected

**Advanced Filtering Patterns:**
- **Interface Pattern Matching**: Complex interface selection with regex and range support
- **Metric-Specific Filtering**: Targeted metric collection for specific analysis requirements
- **Performance Optimized**: Filter patterns optimized for high-performance data retrieval
- **Hierarchical Filtering**: Support for device hierarchies and organizational structures

- **Health Trending**: Track healthy vs unhealthy client ratios over time for capacity planning
- **Anomaly Detection**: Identify sudden changes in client health for automated alerting
- **Historical Analysis**: Review client health patterns for root cause analysis
- **Dashboard Widgets**: Power real-time and historical health visualizations

port congestion, broadcast thresholds, total errors, and IP connectivity for each client event.

post.summary: Client Trail Roaming Data for AI and MCP Servers
post.description:
**Client Roaming Trail Analysis for MCP Servers**

Retrieves roaming trail data from the Historical Client Session table, showing
the sequence of access point transitions (roams) for a specific client within
a given time range. A roam event is detected when the device serial number changes
between consecutive session records sorted by timestamp in ascending order.

**Roam Detection Logic:**
- Sessions are sorted by timestamp ascending for the specified client MAC
- A roam is identified when the device serial number changes between consecutive records
- The "from" fields come from the previous record, "to" fields from the next record
- Roam duration is taken from the `roaming_time` field of the destination (to) record

**Roam Status Determination:**
The status is determined by correlating with the Client Monitor Problem table:
- If any association, authentication, DHCP, DNS, or gateway issue exists for the
  client MAC within the time window → status = `FAILED`
- Otherwise → status = `ROAMING_COMPLETED`

**Problem ID Mapping (from HiveOsProblem):**
- Association issues: problem_id 0–3 (category 1) or -3 (slow association)
- Authentication issues: problem_id 65536–65553 (category 2) or -4 (slow auth)
- DHCP issues: problem_id 131072 or -2 (DHCP slow)
- DNS issues: problem_id 131073
- Gateway issues: problem_id 131074

**Data Sources:**
- `legacy_wireless_historical_client_session_stats` — session records
- `legacy_wireless_client_monitor_problem_stats` — problem/failure detection
- Redis AssetDevice cache — device name and MAC resolution

post.description:
**Client Connectivity Experience Analysis for MCP Servers**

Retrieves the connectivity experience timeline for a specific client, showing
the session-level details including association, authentication, DHCP, DNS, and
gateway status for each connection event within the specified time range.

**Connectivity Flow:**
Each session record represents one connection event. The circle statuses indicate
the outcome of each connectivity phase:
1. **Association** — Did the client successfully associate with the AP?
2. **Authentication** — Did the client pass authentication?
3. **DHCP** — Did the client obtain an IP address?
4. **DNS** — Is DNS resolution functioning?
5. **Gateway** — Is the default gateway reachable?

**Circle Status Determination (from Client Monitor Problem table):**
- `associationCircleStatus`: `FAILED` if problem_id in 0–3 or -3, else `SUCCESS`
- `authCircleStatus`: `FAILED` if problem_id in 65536–65553 or -4, else `SUCCESS`
- `dhcpCircleStatus`: `INVALID` if problem_id in 131072 or -2, else `OK`
- `dnsCircleStatus`: `DISABLED` if problem_id = 131073, else `OK`
- `gatewayCircleStatus`: `DISABLED` if problem_id = 131074, else `OK`

**Data Sources:**
- `legacy_wireless_historical_client_session_stats` — session records
- `legacy_wireless_client_metrics_stats` — DHCP/DNS/gateway IPs and response times
- `legacy_wireless_client_monitor_problem_stats` — circle status derivation
- Redis AssetDevice cache — device name resolution

slower than deviceID. Use deviceID for best performance.

Only one device is accepted per request; comma-separated values are rejected.

deviceID.description:
**Preferred device identifier.** Indexed in all metric tables — fastest query path.
Exactly one of deviceID, deviceUUID, or deviceSerialNumber must be provided.
Only one device is accepted per request; comma-separated values are rejected.

deviceSerialNumber.description:
A single device serial number. Resolved to deviceID via Redis
cache, then indexed lookup. Exactly one of deviceID, deviceUUID, or
deviceSerialNumber must be provided.
Only one device is accepted per request; comma-separated values are rejected.

startTime.description:
Start time for data retrieval in ISO 8601 UTC format. Results include data points
from this time (inclusive). Cannot be used with durationInMinutes alone.

endTime.description:
End time for data retrieval in ISO 8601 UTC format. Results include data points
up to this time (exclusive). Cannot be used with durationInMinutes alone.

durationInMinutes.description:
**Unit: Minutes**

Duration in minutes for data retrieval. Behavior depends on other time parameters:
- Alone: Returns data from 'duration' minutes ago to now
- With startTime: Returns data from startTime for specified duration
- With endTime: Returns data for specified duration before endTime
Cannot be used with both startTime and endTime.

frequency.description:
Data sampling frequency for large datasets:
- NONE: Return all available data points (default)
- ONE_FIFTH: Sample every 5th data point (20% of data)
- ONE_TENTH: Sample every 10th data point (10% of data)

pageNumber.description: Current page number for pagination (1-based indexing)

pageSize.description: Number of items per page. The maximum allowed value is currently 10,000.

errOnPageExceeded.description:
When `true`, a request that would return an item count exceeding the pagination maximum
(currently 10,000) will generate an HTTP status 409 error instead of 200 and pagination information.

filter.description:
Array of filter criteria for refining data selection. Supports complex
interface patterns and metric-specific filtering.

latestValue.description:
When true, retrieves only the most recent data point for each metric.
Useful for real-time monitoring and current status queries.
Overrides time range parameters when enabled.

When latestValue is used with client-related metric groups, the API returns 
only the latest client connected to each device for real-time client connectivity status.

MetricDataResponse.description: Paginated response containing metric data for the requested device and metric group.

metricsInfo.description: Detailed metric data including device identifiers, sampling frequency, and time-series measurements.

paginationInfo.description: Pagination metadata including current page number, page size, and total item/page counts.

MetricDataDetailResponses.title: metric detail responses
MetricDataDetailResponses.description:
Detailed metric data response for a specific device and metric group.
Contains device identifiers, sampling frequency, and time-series metric data points.

ownerID.description: Identifier of the organization or tenant owning this data.

deviceUUID.description: Universally unique identifier for the device in UUID v4 format.

deviceSerialNumber.description: Manufacturer-assigned serial number of the device.

frequency.description: the frequency the metric data is sampled. With default NONE, no sample of data.

metricName.description:
The name of the metric being reported. This is the sub-metric identifier
(e.g. `cpu stats`, `fan stats`, `ethernet interface stats`). Use the
`capabilityRef` field in this response to retrieve the exact field names,
types, and units for this sub-metric.

capabilityRef.description:
URL path to retrieve the detailed field definitions (names, types, units)
for this sub-metric. Perform a GET request to this path to understand how
to interpret the values in `metricData` without prior knowledge of field names.

timeStamp.description: Timestamp of the metric data point in ISO 8601 UTC format.

metricInfo.description:
Array of name-value pairs representing individual metric measurements
for this data point. Each entry contains a metric field name and its
corresponding value. Use the `capabilityRef` in the parent response to
look up field definitions, units, and data types.

NameValue.description:
A name-value pair representing a single metric measurement.
Used in metricInfo arrays to report individual metric readings for network devices.

name.description:
The metric field name identifier. Field names are PascalCase and vary by
sub-metric. For example, `cpu stats` fields include `DeviceCore`, `UsageMax`,
`UsageAvg`, `UsageMin`; `fan stats` fields include `Fan`, `Tray`, `RpmMax`,
`RpmAvg`, `RpmMin`, `PwmMax`, `PwmAvg`, `PwmMin`.

To retrieve the complete list of field names, types, and units for any
sub-metric, call GET on the `capabilityRef` URL returned in the parent
`metricsInfo` object, or call GET /metric-schema for all groups at once.

value.description:
The metric measurement value as a string. The unit depends on the field;
call GET on `capabilityRef` (or GET /metric-schema) to look up units per
field name. Common examples:

- Percentage usage fields such as for cpu or memory (e.g., `UsageMax`, `UsageAvg`, `UsageMin`): `"72.5"` means 72.5%
- RPM fields (e.g., `RpmMax`, `RpmAvg`, `RpmMin`): `"3200"` means 3200 RPM
- Celsisu fields such as for temperature (e.g., `TemperatureMax`, `TemperatureAvg`): `"42.0"` means 42 °C
- Watts fields (e.g., `Capacity`, `InputPowerMax`): `"150.0"` means 150 W
- Ampere fields (e.g., `InputCurrentMax`): `"2.5"` means 2.5 A
- Byte fields (e.g., `RxBytes`, `TxBytes`): `"1048576"` means 1 MiB
- Index fields (e.g., `DeviceCore`, `Fan`, `Tray`, `Unit`): integer index

All numeric values are encoded as strings for consistent JSON serialization.

FilterQuery.title: Filter Query
FilterQuery.description:
Defines filtering criteria for metric data retrieval. Supports various filter types
for precise data selection and interface-specific queries.

type.description:
Type of filter to apply. Each type supports specific value formats:

- **ethernet interface name**: Filter by Ethernet interface patterns
- **device stats**: Filter by specific device statistics
- **wireless interface stats**: Filter by wireless interface metrics

value.description:
Filter value using type-specific format patterns:

**For ethernet interface name:**
- Single interface: "0/1" or "1:1"
- Interface ranges: "0/30-33" or "1:30-33"
- Multiple selections: "0/1,0/30-33,0/12:1-4"
- Stack notation: "1:12:1-4" (stack:slot:port range)

**For ethernet interface ext1 name:**
- Single interface: "0/1" or "1:1"
- Interface ranges: "0/30-33" or "1:30-33"
- Multiple selections: "0/1,0/30-33,0/12:1-4"
- Stack notation: "1:12:1-4" (stack:slot:port range)

**For device stats:**
- Specific stat names: "cpu,memory,temperature"

**For wireless interface stats:**
- Wireless interface identifiers: "wifi0,wifi1"
- Sub-stat filter values: "rf", "client", "rfnbr", "nbrtable", "network", "xif", "radioattr"

**For legacy wireless interface usage stats:**
- Interface identifiers: "2:12"

**For protocol stats:**
- Specific stat names: "lldp nbr port, lldp neighbor, elrp, route summary, isis (isis stats only), isis all (all isis stats), isis int counters, isis int l1 control packet counters, isis stats, cdp, radius, stp, stp port, stp stats"

**For acl stats:**
- Specific stat names: "policy acl, user acl"

ErrorModel.title: Error Response
ErrorModel.description:
Standardized error response format providing detailed information about API failures.
Use the error code for programmatic error handling and the message for user display.

code.description:
Numeric error code indicating the specific type of failure:

**Success Code:**
- 0: No Error (PerfmonSuccess)

**Validation Errors (1000-1099):**
- 1002: Validation Error (PerfmonValidationError) - Invalid input parameters, maps to HTTP 409

**Database Errors (1300-1399):**
- 1301: Database Connection Error (PerfmonConnectionToDatabaseError) - Database at capacity / connection rejected (transient overload), maps to HTTP 503
- 1302: Database Get Error (PerfmonDBGetError) - Data retrieval failure, maps to HTTP 500
- 1303: Database Create Error (PerfmonDBCreateError) - Data creation failure, maps to HTTP 500
- 1304: Database Save Error (PerfmonDBSaveError) - Data save failure, maps to HTTP 500
- 1305: Database Delete Error (PerfmonDBDeleteError) - Data deletion failure, maps to HTTP 500
- 1306: Database Update Error (PerfmonDBUpdateError) - Data update failure, maps to HTTP 500
- 1307: Database Find Error (PerfmonDBFindError) - Data search failure, maps to HTTP 404
- 1308: Database Ping Error (PerfmonDBPingError) - Database connectivity test failure, maps to HTTP 500
- 1309: Database Inconsistent (PerfmonDBInconsistent) - Database state inconsistency, maps to HTTP 500

**API Processing Errors (1700-1799):**
- 1701: API Validation Error (PerfmonAPIValidationError) - Request validation failure, maps to HTTP 400
- 1702: API Decode Error (PerfmonAPIDecodeError) - Request decoding failure, maps to HTTP 400
- 1703: API Unmarshal Error (PerfmonAPIUnmarshalError) - JSON unmarshaling failure, maps to HTTP 400
- 1704: API Marshal Error (PerfmonAPIMarshalError) - JSON marshaling failure, maps to HTTP 500
- 1705: API Write Error (PerfmonAPIWriteError) - Response write failure, maps to HTTP 500
- 1706: API Read Error (PerfmonAPIReadError) - Request read failure, maps to HTTP 400

**Service Conditions (load shedding, not business errors):**
- 1429: Rate Limited (PerfmonRateLimited) - Per-client rate limit exceeded, maps to HTTP 429
- 1503: Service Overloaded (PerfmonServiceOverloaded) - Admission control shed the request or the server-side processing deadline was exceeded, maps to HTTP 503

**Authentication/Authorization Errors (1800-1899):**
- 1838: Request Unauthorized Error (PerfmonRequestUnauthorizedError) - Authentication failure, maps to HTTP 401

**Unknown/Generic Errors:**
- 1: Unknown Error (PerfmonUnknownErr) - Generic unknown error, maps to HTTP 500

Use these codes for automated error handling and monitoring.

message.description:
Human-readable description of the error condition. Provides context-specific
details about what went wrong and may include suggestions for resolution.
message.example: Invalid time format. Use ISO 8601 UTC format (e.g., 2024-08-26T19:00:00Z)

details.description:
Optional additional details about the error condition, such as validation
failures, affected parameters, or debugging information.

items_count.description: The number of items on the current page i.e page size

total_pages.description: The total number of pages available

total_items_count.description: The total number of items across all pages

PortStatsRequest.title: Port Stats Request
PortStatsRequest.description:
Request object for retrieving port statistics for a device
over a specified time range, optionally filtered by interface names.

ifNames.description:
Comma-separated list of interface names to filter (e.g., "ge.1.1,ge.1.2").
If omitted, statistics from all interfaces are included.

startTime.description: Start of the query time range in ISO 8601 UTC format. Required.

endTime.description: End of the query time range in ISO 8601 UTC format. Required. Must be after startTime.

PortStatsDataPoint.title: Port Stats Data Point
PortStatsDataPoint.description:
A single time-stamped row of aggregated port statistics,
representing sums across all matched interfaces at one timestamp.

timestamp.description: Timestamp of this data point in ISO 8601 UTC format.

clientsWithIssues.description: Number of unique clients that experienced connectivity issues on any of the matched interfaces at this timestamp.

totalTxBytes.description: Total transmitted bytes (out_octets) summed across matched interfaces at this timestamp.

totalRxBytes.description: Total received bytes (in_octets) summed across matched interfaces at this timestamp.

totalErrors.description: Total error count (errors_in_errors + errors_out_errors) at this timestamp.

totalQueueCongestion.description: Total queue congestion packets dropped across all queues (Q0–Q15) at this timestamp.

PortStatsResponse.title: Port Stats Response
PortStatsResponse.description:
Array of time-stamped port statistics data points, ordered by timestamp ascending.
Each element represents statistics summed across all matched interfaces at one timestamp.

PortStatsSummaryRequest.title: Port Stats Summary Request
PortStatsSummaryRequest.description: Request object for retrieving the per-port statistics summary for a device.

deviceId.description: Numeric identifier of the device whose port summary is requested.

PortStatsSummaryItem.title: Port Stats Summary Item
PortStatsSummaryItem.description: Per-port statistics summary for a single port on the device.

rxUtilization.description: Average receive utilization as a percentage over the query period.

txUtilization.description: Average transmit utilization as a percentage over the query period.

rxMaxUtilization.description: Maximum receive utilization observed (percentage) during the query period.

txMaxUtilization.description: Maximum transmit utilization observed (percentage) during the query period.

inOctets.description: Total inbound bytes on this port.

outOctets.description: Total outbound bytes on this port.

inUcastPkts.description: Total inbound unicast packets on this port.

outUcastPkts.description: Total outbound unicast packets on this port.

inBroadcastPkts.description: Total inbound broadcast packets on this port.

outBroadcastPkts.description: Total outbound broadcast packets on this port.

inMulticastPkts.description: Total inbound multicast packets on this port.

outMulticastPkts.description: Total outbound multicast packets on this port.

congestionDropPkts.description: Total packets dropped on this port due to queue congestion.

totalAggregateErrors.description: Total aggregate error count (input errors + output errors) on this port.

PortStatsSummaryResponse.title: Port Stats Summary Response
PortStatsSummaryResponse.description: Array of per-port statistics summary items. Each element represents one port on the device.

DeviceHealthDataRequest.title: Wired Device Health Data Request
DeviceHealthDataRequest.description:
Request object for retrieving comprehensive health analytics for wired network devices.
Supports hierarchical location filtering and configurable health metric selection.

siteIDs.description:
Comma-separated list of site identifiers for location-based filtering.
Sites represent the highest level in the location hierarchy (e.g., campus, datacenter).
Use this to filter devices by geographical or organizational sites.
Supports up to approximately 200 site IDs per request for optimal performance.

buildingIDs.description:
Comma-separated list of building identifiers within the specified sites.
Buildings represent physical structures or logical groupings within sites.
More specific than site-level filtering.
Supports up to approximately 200 building IDs per request for optimal performance.

floorIDs.description:
Comma-separated list of floor identifiers within the specified buildings.
Floors represent the most granular level of location-based filtering,
useful for maintenance and physical access planning.
Supports up to approximately 200 floor IDs per request for optimal performance.

deviceIDs.description:
Comma-separated list of specific wired device identifiers to retrieve health data for.
Use this to target individual devices regardless of their location.

deviceStats.description:
Comma-separated list of health metric categories to include in the response.
Controls which health parameters are collected and returned.

**Available Metrics:**
- **cpu**: Processor utilization percentage (0-100%)
- **memory**: RAM usage percentage (0-100%)
- **temperature**: Thermal readings in degrees Celsius (°C)
- **fan**: Cooling system speed in RPM and operational status
- **poe**: Power over Ethernet consumption in watts (W)
- **psu**: Power supply unit output in watts (W) and operational status
- **macaddress**: MAC address table utilization percentage (0-100%)

If not specified, returns all available metrics by default.

health.description:
Filter devices by health status.

**Available Statuses:**
- **unhealthy**: Devices with one or more health issues

If not specified, returns devices of all health statuses by default.

responseType.description:
Controls the format of the response data:
- `summary`: Returns aggregated health summary statistics only
- `grid`: Returns detailed per-device health information in grid format

deviceType.description: **Deprecated — do not use.** The api will return all wired network devices if it is set to wired or empty. For wireless it will return an empty result.

managedBy.description:
Filter by management type of device as specified below -
**Available Types:**
- **cloud**: Response contains health information for cloud managed devices
- **TPME**: Response contains health information for third party managed devices

If not specified, returns health information for both cloud and on-premises managed devices by default.

sortField.description:
An optional field by which to sort device health data. If specified, may be: "hostName", "siteName", "cpu",
"memory", "temperature", "fan", "psu", or "poe".

sortOrder.description: Order to sort the device health data. Can be ascending or descending.

keyword.description:
Keyword to filter the device health data. Matches against device hostName,
ip address, MAC address, site name, building name and floor name.

pageNumber.description:
Current page number for pagination using 1-based indexing.
Use this in combination with pageSize to navigate through large device inventories.

pageSize.description:
Number of devices to return per page. Recommended maximum is 100 for optimal
performance, though the system supports up to 1000 devices per page.

metricGroup.description: The metric group category this response belongs to (e.g., device health).

ownerID.description: Identifier of the organization or tenant owning this data.

summaryInfo.description: Aggregated summary statistics of device health across all filtered devices, including counts of total, unhealthy, and issue-specific devices.

healthInfo.description: Detailed health information for individual devices, including per-device metrics and stack membership data.

HealthInfo.description: Detailed health information for individual devices, including per-device metrics and stack membership data.

paginationInfo.description: Pagination metadata for navigating through large result sets, including current page, page size, and total counts.

HealthInfoItem.description: Comprehensive device metrics including identification, location, configuration, and health data for a single device.

metricsInfo.description: Detailed metric information including device identifiers, metric names, and health data.

deviceUUID.description: Universally unique identifier for the device in UUID v4 format.

deviceSerialNumber.description: Manufacturer-assigned serial number of the device.

macAddress.description: MAC address of the device (uppercase hex without delimiters).

ipAddress.description:
IP address of the device. Supports both IPv4 and IPv6 formats.
For IPv6, use standard RFC 5952 text representation (may include `::` compression).

stackLocation.description:
Physical location of the device within a stack configuration.
Format: "Site name:Building name:Floor name" (e.g., "San Jose Campus-SJ-Building-1-Floor-3" ).
Only populated for devices that are part of a stack.

function.description: The functional role of the network device.

managedBy.description: Indicates how the device is managed.

stackType.description:
Indicates whether the device is part of a stack configuration.
True if the device is stacked, false if it is standalone.

stackNumber.description:
The position number of the device within a stack (1-based).
Only meaningful when stackType is true.

stackMode.description:
The operational role of the device within a stack configuration.

**Available Stack Modes:**
- **PRIMARY**: Primary/active controller in a stack — manages stack coordination and configuration distribution
- **BACKUP_IN_SYNC**: Backup controller synchronized with PRIMARY — ready for immediate failover
- **STANDBY**: Standby device in the stack — available for failover but may not be fully synchronized
- **MEMBER**: Secondary device participating in a stack — forwards traffic under PRIMARY control
- **MASTER**: Legacy term for the primary controller role (older firmware devices)
- **STANDALONE**: Device operating independently, not part of any stack configuration
- **switch_stack**: Device is operating as part of a switch stack group
- **NONE**: No stack mode assigned or not applicable for this device

stackSize.description:
Total number of devices in the stack.
Only meaningful when stackType is true.

siteID.description: Identifier of the site where the device is located.

deviceHealthData.description: Collection of health metrics for the device, each entry representing a specific metric type (CPU, memory, temperature, fan, PSU, or PoE) captured at a specific timestamp.

stackMembershipInfo.description: Array of stack member device data (only populated for stack master devices)

parentStackMemberName.description: Display name of the stack master device to which this member belongs.

stackDisplayName.description:
Display name for the stack, can be different from the stack name.
Only populated for stack master devices.

stackCpuMax.description:
Maximum CPU usage percentage across all stack members.
Computed as max of per-member average CPU usage. Capped at 100.
Only populated for stack master devices.

stackCpuAvg.description:
Average CPU usage percentage across all stack members.
Computed as avg of per-member average CPU usage. Capped at 100.
Only populated for stack master devices.

stackMemoryMax.description:
Maximum memory usage percentage across all stack members.
Computed as max of per-member memory usage. Capped at 100.
Only populated for stack master devices.

stackMemoryAvg.description:
Average memory usage percentage across all stack members.
Computed as avg of per-member memory usage. Capped at 100.
Only populated for stack master devices.

stackTemperatureMax.description:
Maximum temperature value (°C) across all stack members.
Computed as max of per-member max temperature.
Only populated for stack master devices.

stackTemperatureAvg.description:
Average temperature value (°C) across all stack members.
Computed as avg of per-member max temperature.
Only populated for stack master devices.

stackPsuMax.description:
Maximum PSU output power (watts) across all stack members.
Only populated for stack master devices.

stackPsuAvg.description:
Average PSU output power (watts) across all stack members.
Only populated for stack master devices.

stackPoeTotalBudget.description:
Total PoE power budget (watts) across all stack members.
Calculated as 740W × number of stack members.
Only populated for stack master devices.

stackPoeTotalConsumed.description:
Total PoE power consumed (watts) across all stack members.
Calculated as sum of (per-member consumed percent × per-member budget / 100).
Only populated for stack master devices.

stackCpuStatus.description:
Overall CPU health status for the stack.
Aggregated from all stack members. Only populated for stack parent devices.

stackMemoryStatus.description:
Overall memory health status for the stack.
Aggregated from all stack members. Only populated for stack parent devices.

stackTemperatureStatus.description:
Overall temperature health status for the stack.
Aggregated from all stack members. Only populated for stack parent devices.

stackPoeStatus.description:
Overall PoE health status for the stack.
Aggregated from all stack members. Only populated for stack parent devices.

stackFanStatus.description:
Global aggregated fan health status across all stack members.
Only populated for stack master devices.
Values: "ok" (all fans operational), "critical" (at least one fan non-operational).

stackPSUStatus.description:
Global aggregated PSU health status across all stack members
Only populated for stack master devices.
Values: "ok" (all PSUs operational), "critical" (at least one PSU non-operational).

StackPoeTotalConsumedPercent.description:
Total PoE power consumed as a percentage of total budget across all stack members.
Calculated as (stackPoeTotalConsumed / stackPoeTotalBudget) × 100.
Only populated for stack master devices.

metricName.description:
The name of the health metric being reported, corresponding to the
deviceStats values from the request.

timeStamp.description:
Timestamp of when the health metric was collected. Uses ISO 8601 date-time format in UTC,
indicated by the `Z` suffix (e.g., `2024-08-26T19:00:00Z`).

healthStatus.description: Overall health status for this metric: green (healthy), orange (warning), red (critical).

healthValue.description: Aggregated health value for this metric. For CPU/memory, represents percentage (0-100); for temperature, degrees Celsius; for fan/psu, operational count.

macAddressHealthInfo.description: array of MAC address table health information

StackMemberData.description: Health and metrics data for a stack member device

deviceUUID.description: Universally unique identifier for the stack member device in UUID v4 format.

deviceSerialNumber.description: Manufacturer-assigned serial number of the device.

macAddress.description: MAC address of the device (uppercase hex without delimiters).

ipAddress.description: IP address of the device. Supports both IPv4 and IPv6 formats.

function.description: The functional role of the network device.

managedBy.description: Indicates how the device is managed.

productType.description: Product type of the device (e.g., Switch-5720-48P, X440_G2_48t_10_G4).

stackType.description:
Indicates whether the device is part of a stack configuration.
True if the device is stacked, false if it is standalone.

stackNumber.description: The position number of the device within a stack (1-based).

stackMode.description: The role of the device within a stack configuration.

stackSize.description: Total number of devices in the stack.

stackMemberType.description: The node type of the stack member (e.g., PRIMARY, BACKUP_IN_SYNC, STANDBY).

stackMemberName.description: Display name for the stack member (e.g., "Member 1", "Member 2").

siteID.description: Identifier of the site where the device is located.

deviceHealthData.description: Health metrics for this stack member

fanStatus.description:
Aggregated fan health status for this stack member.
Values: "ok" (all fans operational), "critical" (at least one fan non-operational).

cpuUsagePercent.description: Average CPU usage percentage for this stack member across all cores. Capped at 100.

memoryUsagePercent.description: Average memory usage percentage for this stack member. Capped at 100.

temperatureValue.description: Maximum temperature value (°C) for this stack member across all sensors.

psuOutputPower.description: Maximum PSU output power (watts) for this stack member across all PSU units.

poeTotalBudget.description: Total PoE power budget (watts) for this stack member. Default is 740W per device.

poeTotalConsumedPercent.description: Maximum PoE power consumed percentage for this stack member. Capped at 100.

poeTotalConsumed.description:
Actual PoE power consumed (watts) for this stack member from device telemetry.
When available, this is the real consumed value from the device rather than
a computed value from percent × budget.

cpuStatus.description: CPU health status for this individual stack member.

memoryStatus.description: Memory health status for this individual stack member.

temperatureStatus.description: Temperature health status for this individual stack member.

poeStatus.description: PoE health status for this individual stack member.

psuStatus.description:
PSU operational status for this individual stack member.
Derived from the PSU status reported by the device.
- **ok**: All PSU units are operational.
- **critical**: At least one PSU unit is non-operational.
- **N/A**: No PSU data available for this member.

cpuUsage.description: CPU utilization percentage for this core (0-100%).

status.description: Health status for this CPU core: green (normal), orange (warning), red (critical).
Memory health status: green (normal), orange (warning), red (critical).

temperature.description: Device temperature reading in degrees Celsius (°C).

status.description: Temperature health status: green (normal), orange (warning), red (critical).

fan.description: Fan unit identifier/number within the device.

tray.description: Fan tray identifier (e.g., A, B, C) indicating physical location within the device.

status.description: Fan operational status: operational (functioning normally), non-operational (failed or not running).

unit.description: Power Supply Unit (PSU) identifier/number within the device.

status.description: PSU operational status: operational (functioning normally), non-operational (failed).

totalPowerConsumedPercent.description: Total PoE power consumed as a percentage of total PoE budget (0-100%).

status.description: PoE health status: green (normal usage), orange (high usage warning), red (critical/overload).

macAddressHealth.description:
MAC address table utilization metrics for network devices.
Provides visibility into forwarding table capacity usage.

currentCount.description: Current number of MAC addresses in the device's forwarding table.

totalCapacity.description: Maximum number of MAC addresses the forwarding table can hold.

utilization.description: MAC address table utilization as a percentage (0-100%). Calculated as (currentCount / totalCapacity) × 100.

status.description: MAC address table health status: green (< 60% utilization), yellow (60-79% utilization), red (≥ 80% utilization).

UsageCapacityDataRequest.title: Usage Capacity Data Request
UsageCapacityDataRequest.description:
Request object for retrieving comprehensive usage capacity analytics for network devices.
Supports hierarchical location filtering and configurable usage capacity metric selection.

siteIDs.description:
Comma-separated list of site identifiers for location-based filtering.
Sites represent the highest level in the location hierarchy (e.g., campus, datacenter).
Use this to filter devices by geographical or organizational sites.
Supports up to approximately 200 site IDs per request for optimal performance.

buildingIDs.description:
Comma-separated list of building identifiers within the specified sites.
Buildings represent physical structures or logical groupings within sites.
More specific than site-level filtering.
Supports up to approximately 200 building IDs per request for optimal performance.

floorIDs.description:
Comma-separated list of floor identifiers within the specified buildings.
Floors represent the most granular level of location-based filtering,
useful for maintenance and physical access planning.
Supports up to approximately 200 floor IDs per request for optimal performance.

deviceIDs.description:
Comma-separated list of specific device identifiers to retrieve usage capacity data for.
Use this to target individual devices regardless of their location.

responseType.description:
Type of response as specified below -
**Available Types:**
- **summary**: Response contains usage capacity summary for site/building/floor
- **grid**: Response contains usage capacity information of each device

If not specified, returns usage capacity summary by default.

deviceType.description:
Type of device as specified below -
**Available Types:**
- **wired**: Response contains usage capacity information for wired devices on site/building/floor
- **wireless**: Response contains usage capacity information for wireless devices on site/building/floor

If not specified, returns usage capacity information for both wired and wireless devices by default.

managedBy.description:
Filter by management type of device as specified below -
**Available Types:**
- **cloud**: Response contains usage capacity information for cloud managed devices
- **TPME**: Response contains usage capacity information for third party managed devices

If not specified, returns usage capacity information for both cloud and on-premises managed devices by default.

haveQueueCongestionPackets.description:
When `true`, only those devices with totalQueueCongestionPackets values > 0 are returned in the results.

ClientHealthDataRequest.title: Wired client Health Data Request
ClientHealthDataRequest.description:
Request object for retrieving comprehensive health analytics for wired client devices.
Supports hierarchical location filtering and configurable health metric selection.

siteIDs.description:
Comma-separated list of site identifiers for location-based filtering.
Sites represent the highest level in the location hierarchy (e.g., campus, datacenter).
Use this to filter devices by geographical or organizational sites.
Supports up to approximately 200 site IDs per request for optimal performance.

buildingIDs.description:
Comma-separated list of building identifiers within the specified sites.
Buildings represent physical structures or logical groupings within sites.
More specific than site-level filtering.
Supports up to approximately 200 building IDs per request for optimal performance.

floorIDs.description:
Comma-separated list of floor identifiers within the specified buildings.
Floors represent the most granular level of location-based filtering,
useful for maintenance and physical access planning.
Supports up to approximately 200 floor IDs per request for optimal performance.

deviceIDs.description:
Comma-separated list of specific wired device identifiers to retrieve health data for.
Use this to target individual wired devices regardless of their location.

clientMac.description:
A single wired client MAC address to retrieve health data for.
Use this to target an individual client regardless of its location.
The MAC address must be a 12-character uppercase hexadecimal string (e.g., B8D5467711C0).

filter.description:
Comma-separated list of client stats filters to include clients with these health
issues in the response.

**Note:** This filter applies only when `responseType` is `grid`. It is ignored
when `responseType` is `summary` — the summary counts always reflect all clients
regardless of this filter.

**Available Client Stats:**
- **port-congestion-healthy**: Represents low utilization or healthy state on network ports
- **port-congestion-unhealthy**: Represents high utilization or saturation on network ports
- **ip-connectivity-valid-ip**: Indicates clients with valid IP addresses and good connectivity
- **ip-connectivity-self-assigned-ip**: Indicates clients with self-assigned IP addresses, which may suggest DHCP issues
- **ip-connectivity-unassigned-ip**: Indicates clients without assigned IP addresses, which may suggest connectivity issues
- **traffic-anomalies-unhealthy**: Detects unusual or unexpected traffic patterns
- **traffic-anomalies-healthy**: Indicates normal traffic patterns without anomalies
- **port-errors-unhealthy**: Captures error events on network ports
- **port-errors-healthy**: Indicates absence of error events on network ports
- **client-unhealthy**: Represents clients with overall unhealthy status based on aggregated metrics
- **connected**: Return only clients that are currently connected to the network
- **disconnected**: Return only clients that have recently disconnected (within 24 hours) from the network

If neither `connected` nor `disconnected` is specified, defaults to both (all clients are returned regardless of connection status).
`connected` and `disconnected` are mutually exclusive — do not combine them.

responseType.description:
Type of response as specified below -
**Available Types:**
- **summary**: Response contains processor health summary for site/building/floor
- **grid**: Health information of clients for each metrics

If not specified, returns health summary by default.

deviceType.description: **Deprecated — do not use.** The api will return all wired client devices if it is set to wired or empty. For wireless it will return an empty result.

managedBy.description:
Filter by management type of device as specified below -
**Available Types:**
- **cloud**: Response contains client health information for cloud managed devices
- **TPME**: Response contains client health information for third party managed devices

If not specified, returns client health information for both cloud and on-premises managed devices by default.

sortField.description:
An optional field by which to sort client health data. If specified, may be: "connectionStatus", "client", "location", "ipv4",
"port-number", "vlan", "operating-system", "mac", "user-name", "instant-port-profile", "total-congestion",
"total-unicast", "total-multicast", "total-broadcast" or "ipv6".

sortOrder.description: Order to sort the client health data. Can be ascending or descending.

keyword.description:
Keyword to filter the client health data. Matches against client, location,
port number, switch name, vlan and operating system etc.

**Note:** This filter applies only when `responseType` is `grid`. It is ignored
when `responseType` is `summary` — the summary counts always reflect all clients
regardless of this filter.

pageNumber.description:
Current page number for pagination using 1-based indexing.
Use this in combination with pageSize to navigate through large client inventories.

pageSize.description:
Number of clients to return per page. Recommended maximum is 100 for optimal
performance, though the system supports up to 1000 clients per page.

ClientHealthStatsRequest.title: Client Health Stats Request
ClientHealthStatsRequest.description:
Request object for retrieving client health stats time-series data.
Supports latest-value queries and historical time-range queries with automatic
aggregation tier selection for optimal performance.

deviceID.description:
Internal device ID to retrieve client health stats for.
One device ID is required.

startTime.description:
Start time for data retrieval in ISO 8601 UTC format. Results include data points
from this time (inclusive). Required when `latestValue` is false.
The system automatically selects the optimal aggregation tier based on the time span.

endTime.description:
End time for data retrieval in ISO 8601 UTC format. Results include data points
up to this time (exclusive). Required when `latestValue` is false.

latestValue.description:
When true, retrieves only the most recent data point from the base hypertable
for each requested device. Overrides time range parameters when enabled.
Useful for real-time dashboards and current status monitoring.

pageNumber.description: Current page number for pagination (1-based indexing).

pageSize.description: Number of data points to return per page. Maximum allowed value is 1000.

ClientHealthStatsResponses.description: Response containing client health stats time-series data with pagination.

ownerID.description: Identifier of the organization or tenant owning this data.

Array of client health stats data points ordered by timestamp ascending.
Each data point represents the healthy and unhealthy client counts for a device
at a specific point in time.

ClientHealthStatsDataPoint.description: A single time-series data point representing client health counts for a device.

ts.description:
Timestamp of the data point in ISO 8601 UTC format.
Granularity depends on the aggregation tier selected based on the query time range.

healthyClients.description:
Number of healthy clients connected to this device at the given timestamp.
A client is considered healthy when its port has no congestion drops, no errors,
broadcast percentage is within threshold, and the client has valid IP connectivity.

unhealthyClients.description:
Number of unhealthy clients connected to this device at the given timestamp.
A client is considered unhealthy if any of the following conditions are met:
- Port not found in port stats
- Missing IP information (no IPv4 or IP address)
- Port congestion drop packets > 0
- Broadcast percentage exceeds threshold of 75
- Total port errors > 0

WirelessDeviceHealthDataRequest.title: Wireless Device Health Data Request
WirelessDeviceHealthDataRequest.description: Request object for retrieving health analytics exclusively for wireless (AP) network devices.

Controls which health parameters are collected and returned.

**Available Metrics:**
- **cpu**: Processor utilization percentage (0-100%)
- **memory**: RAM usage percentage (0-100%)
- **poe**: Power over Ethernet consumption in watts (W)

If not specified, returns all available metrics by default.

Filter devices by health status.

**Available Statuses:**
- **unhealthy**: Wireless devices with one or more health issues
- **not-reporting**: Wireless devices with no stats data available

If not specified, returns devices of all health statuses by default.

Controls the format of the response data:
- `summary`: Returns aggregated health summary statistics only
- `grid`: Returns detailed per-device health information in grid format

has_memory_usage_issues.description: When true, filters results to only include devices that have memory usage issues exceeding the configured threshold.

has_poe_usage_issues.description: When true, filters results to only include devices that have PoE usage issues exceeding the configured threshold.

numberFilter.description:
Array of numeric filter conditions to apply on metric columns.
Each filter specifies a column name, a comparison operator, and the value(s) to compare against.

**Supported filter types:**
- **eq**: Equal to — matches rows where column equals `value`
- **neq**: Not equal to — matches rows where column does not equal `value`
- **gt**: Greater than — matches rows where column is greater than `value`
- **gte**: Greater than or equal to — matches rows where column >= `value`
- **lt**: Less than — matches rows where column < `value`
- **lte**: Less than or equal to — matches rows where column <= `value`
- **btw**: Between — matches rows where column is between `min` and `max` (inclusive)

NumberFilterItem.title: Number Filter Item
NumberFilterItem.description:

and `min`/`max` for range comparisons (btw).

columnName.description: The name of the metric column to filter on.

The unit corresponds to the selected columnName: percentage (0-100) for cpu, memory, poe; dimensionless score for eth0/eth1 metrics.

min.description:
The minimum value for range filtering. Used with filter_type "btw".
The unit corresponds to the selected columnName: percentage (0-100) for cpu, memory, poe; dimensionless score for eth0/eth1 metrics.

max.description:
The maximum value for range filtering. Used with filter_type "btw".
The unit corresponds to the selected columnName: percentage (0-100) for cpu, memory, poe; dimensionless score for eth0/eth1 metrics.

- **roaming-issues**: Filter by client roaming status (show/hide)
- **connection-status**: Filter by client connection status (connected/disconnected)
- **authentication**: Filter by client authentication method (e.g., PSK, 802.1X)

value.description:

WirelessClientHealthDataRequest.title: Wireless Client Health Data Request
WirelessClientHealthDataRequest.description:
Request object for retrieving comprehensive health analytics for wireless clients.
Supports hierarchical location filtering and configurable health metric selection.

siteIDs.description:
Comma-separated list of site identifiers for location-based filtering.
Sites represent the highest level in the location hierarchy (e.g., campus, datacenter).
Use this to filter devices by geographical or organizational sites.
Supports up to approximately 200 site IDs per request for optimal performance.

buildingIDs.description:
Comma-separated list of building identifiers within the specified sites.
Buildings represent physical structures or logical groupings within sites.
More specific than site-level filtering.
Supports up to approximately 200 building IDs per request for optimal performance.

floorIDs.description:
Comma-separated list of floor identifiers within the specified buildings.
Floors represent the most granular level of location-based filtering,
useful for maintenance and physical access planning.
Supports up to approximately 200 floor IDs per request for optimal performance.

deviceIDs.description:
Comma-separated list of specific device identifiers to retrieve health data for.
Use this to target individual devices regardless of their location.

clientMac.description:
A single client MAC address to retrieve health data for.
Use this to target an individual client regardless of its location.
The MAC address must be a 12-character uppercase hexadecimal string (e.g., B8D5467711C0).

responseType.description:
Type of response as specified below -
**Available Types:**
- **summary**: Response contains processor health summary for site/building/floor
- **grid**: Health information of clients for each metrics

If not specified, returns health summary by default.

managedBy.description:
Filter by management type of device as specified below -
**Available Types:**
- **cloud**: Response contains client health information for cloud managed devices
- **TPME**: Response contains client health information for third party managed devices

If not specified, returns client health information for both cloud and on-premises managed devices by default.

health.description:
Filter clients by health status as specified below -
**Available Statuses:**
- **unhealthy**: Response contains client health information for unhealthy clients only

If not specified, returns client health information for clients of all health statuses by default.

filter.description: Array of filter conditions to apply on the client health data. Each filter specifies values in the enum below.

numberFilter.description:
Array of numeric filter conditions to apply on metric columns.
Each filter specifies a column name, a comparison operator, and the value(s) to compare against.

**Supported filter types:**
- **eq**: Equal to — matches rows where column equals `value`
- **neq**: Not equal to — matches rows where column does not equal `value`
- **gt**: Greater than — matches rows where column is greater than `value`
- **gte**: Greater than or equal to — matches rows where column >= `value`
- **lt**: Less than — matches rows where column < `value`
- **lte**: Less than or equal to — matches rows where column <= `value`
- **btw**: Between — matches rows where column is between `min` and `max` (inclusive)

sortField.description: An optional field by which to sort client health data.

sortOrder.description: Order to sort the client health data. Can be ascending or descending.

keyword.description:
Keyword to filter the client health data. Matches against client, location,
etc.

pageNumber.description:
Current page number for pagination using 1-based indexing.
Use this in combination with pageSize to navigate through large client inventories.

pageSize.description:
Number of clients to return per page. Recommended maximum is 100 for optimal
performance, though the system supports up to 1000 clients per page.

WirelessUsageCapacityDataRequest.description:
Request parameters for wireless usage capacity data retrieval.

ownerID.description: Identifier of the organization or tenant owning this data.

pageSize.description: Number of records to return per page. Use in conjunction with pageNumber for pagination.

pageNumber.description:
Current page number for pagination using 1-based indexing
(e.g., pageNumber=2 with pageSize=50 returns records 51-100).

keyword.description:
Keyword to filter wireless usage capacity data. Matches against device hostName,
IP address, MAC address, site name, building name and floor name.

sortField.description: An optional field by which to sort wireless usage capacity data.

sortOrder.description: Order to sort the wireless usage capacity data. Can be ascending or descending.

responseType.description:
Type of response data to return:
- `grid`: Returns paginated device-level usage capacity data
- `summary`: Returns only summary widgets (channel utilization, retries, packet loss)
- `all`: Returns both summary and grid data

managedBy.description: Indicates how the device is managed.

siteIDs.description: Comma-separated list of site IDs to filter by

buildingIDs.description: Comma-separated list of building IDs to filter by

floorIDs.description: Comma-separated list of floor IDs to filter by

deviceIDs.description: Comma-separated list of specific wireless device identifiers to retrieve health data for.

has_retries_issues.description: When true, filters results to only include devices that have retry rate issues exceeding the configured threshold.

has_packet_loss_issues.description: When true, filters results to only include devices that have packet loss issues exceeding the configured threshold.

has_usage_capacity_issues.description: When true, filters results to only include devices that have usage capacity issues exceeding the configured threshold.

has_2dot4g_utilization_issues.description: Filter devices that have 2.4GHz channel utilization issues exceeding the configured threshold

has_5g_utilization_issues.description: Filter devices that have 5GHz channel utilization issues exceeding the configured threshold

has_6g_utilization_issues.description: Filter devices that have 6GHz channel utilization issues exceeding the configured threshold

haveIssues.description:
When `true`, only wireless devices with at least one issue are returned. Issues include
retries, packet loss, channel utilization, interference, or noise exceeding configured
thresholds on any radio, and unhealthy client count > 0. This is a strict superset
of `has_usage_capacity_issues`.

numberFilter.description:
Column-level number filters for various metrics. Supports filtering at child column level
for Packet Loss, Channel Utilization, Retries, Unicast/Multicast/Broadcast, Noise, and Interference.

columnName.description: The specific metric column to filter on at child column level.

filterType.description: The type of comparison to apply.

min.description: Minimum value for 'between' filter_type. The unit corresponds to the selected columnName (percentage for cpu/memory/utilization, dBm for noise, dimensionless score for other metrics).

max.description: Maximum value for 'between' filter_type. The unit corresponds to the selected columnName (percentage for cpu/memory/utilization, dBm for noise, dimensionless score for other metrics).

value.description: Value for single-value filter types (eq, neq, gt, gte, lt, lte). The unit corresponds to the selected columnName (percentage for cpu/memory/utilization, dBm for noise, dimensionless score for other metrics).

rssi.description: Received Signal Strength Indicator (dBm) of the neighboring access point.

mode.description: Operating mode of the neighboring access point (e.g., "802.11ax", "802.11ac").

rogueAp.description: Rogue AP classification score (0 = not rogue).

extremeDevice.description: Whether this is an Extreme Networks device.

crc.description: CRC error count observed from the neighboring access point.

clients.description: Number of clients connected to the neighboring access point.

Paginated response containing time-series data points for a wireless interface,
ordered by timestamp ascending.

items.description: Array of time-series graph data points.

paginationInfo.description: Pagination metadata for navigating through large result sets.

channelUtilization.description: Channel utilization percentage at this timestamp.

connectedClients.description: Number of clients connected at this timestamp.

startTime.description: Start of the query time range in ISO 8601 UTC format. Required.

endTime.description: End of the query time range in ISO 8601 UTC format. Required. Must be after startTime.

WirelessInterfacesResponse.title: Wireless Interfaces Response
WirelessInterfacesResponse.description:
Map of radio interface names (e.g., wifi0, wifi1, wifi2) to their
interface details including SSID info, client counts, channel
configuration, utilization breakdown, and feature flags.

WirelessInterfaceDetail.description: Detailed information for a single wireless radio interface.

ssidCount.description: Number of SSIDs configured on this radio interface.

ssids.description: List of SSID names configured on this radio interface.

numberOfClients.description: Number of clients currently connected to this radio interface.

channelUtilization.description: Overall channel utilization percentage for this radio interface.

channel.description: Operating channel number for this radio interface.

channelWidth.description: Channel width in MHz for this radio interface.

loadBalancing.description: Whether load balancing is enabled on this radio interface.

bandSteering.description: Whether band steering is enabled on this radio interface.

ChannelUtilizationDetails.description: Breakdown of channel utilization into interference, TX retries, and RX retries.

interferencePercentage.description: Percentage of channel utilization attributed to interference.

txRetriesPercentage.description: Percentage of channel utilization attributed to transmit retries.

rxRetriesPercentage.description: Percentage of channel utilization attributed to receive retries.

startTime.description: Start of the query time range in ISO 8601 UTC format. Required.

endTime.description: End of the query time range in ISO 8601 UTC format. Required. Must be after startTime.

WiredInterfacesResponse.title: Wired Interfaces Response
WiredInterfacesResponse.description:
Response containing an array of wired interface entries for a wireless device,
including port state, traffic counters, and error/drop statistics.

paginationInfo.description: Pagination metadata for navigating through large result sets.

WiredInterfaceItem.description: Detailed information for a single wired interface on a wireless device.

state.description: Operational state of the interface (e.g., up, down).

adminState.description: Administrative state of the interface (e.g., enabled, disabled).

txBytes.description: Total bytes transmitted on this interface.

rxBytes.description: Total bytes received on this interface.

txErrors.description: Total transmit errors on this interface.

rxErrors.description: Total receive errors on this interface.

txDrops.description: Total transmit drops on this interface.

rxDrops.description: Total receive drops on this interface.

powerDraw.description:
PoE power drawn by the device in Watts, as reported via the device's PoE interface.
This is a device-level value (same for all wired interface entries on the same device).
Omitted when the value is not available (e.g., non-PoE device or data not yet received).

clientId.description:

Null when the session is still active.

deviceId.description: Numeric identifier of the device (switch) where the client was connected.

usage.description: Total bytes transferred during this session.

ifName.description: Interface (port) name on the device where the client was connected.

speed.description: Port link speed during this session, expressed in Mbps (e.g., SPEED_1000M = 1000 Mbps).

portDuplex.description: Port duplex mode during this session.

roamStatus.description:
Roaming status of the client at the end of this session.

rssi.description: Received Signal Strength Indicator from the client's perspective, in dBm.

noiseFloor.description: Ambient noise level on the wireless channel, in dBm.

IpRoutingDeviceResponse.title: IP Routing Device Response
IpRoutingDeviceResponse.description: Response containing IPv4 routing details for a device with pagination.

data.description: List of routing data entries for the device.

pagination.description: Pagination metadata for the response, including current page, page size, and total counts.

IpRoutingDeviceData.title: IP Routing Device Data
IpRoutingDeviceData.description: Routing data for a device including refresh timestamps and IPv4 routing entries.

earliest_refresh_time.description: Earliest refresh time of the routing data as raw XIQ timestamp string (format "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.sss"). Empty string if not available.

latest_refresh_time.description: Latest refresh time of the routing data as raw XIQ timestamp string (format "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.sss"). Empty string if not available.

latest_refresh_timestamp.description: Latest refresh time as milliseconds since Unix epoch (UTC). 0 if not available.

ipv4_routing_details.description: List of IPv4 routing table entries.

Ipv4RoutingDetail.title: IPv4 Routing Detail
Ipv4RoutingDetail.description: A single IPv4 routing table entry with next-hop and ping protection information.

vlan_id.description: VLAN identifier associated with the route.

vlan_name.description: VLAN name associated with the route.

route_origin.description: Origin of the route (e.g., BOOTP, DIRECT, OSPF, STATIC, BGP).

status.description: Current operational status of the route.

metric.description: Route metric value representing routing cost (unitless integer; protocol-specific cost units).

age.description: Age of the route in seconds.

route_type_priority.description: Priority value for the route type.

nexthop_ipv4_address.description: IPv4 address of the next hop.

nexthop_device_id.description: Device ID of the next-hop device (0 if unknown).

nexthop_host_name.description: Hostname of the next-hop device (empty if unknown).

ping_protection_enabled.description: Whether ping protection is enabled for this route.

ping_protection_last_uptime.description: Time of last ping protection up event as milliseconds since Unix epoch (UTC). 0 if never observed.

ping_protection_last_downtime.description: Time of last ping protection down event as milliseconds since Unix epoch (UTC). 0 if never observed.
